text:
Priya K.: Quick follow-up from today's infra section 14 folks asked for clearer rules on GPU inventory and autoscale fallbacks. Posting the notes + ask for owners to confirm.

Ben T.: Short summary: H100 headroom is tight in eu-west3 for the next 24 weeks; us-west1 A10G capacity is healthy. Procurement ETA depends on supplier cycle. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

Sam R.: Can we have the explicit fallback chain? e.g., if eu-west3 H100s are gone, do we route to us-west1 A10G with quantized model, or prefer smaller in-region model?

Marta L.: Current policy: prefer_local_capacity is true by default. Fallback order for latency-sensitive routes: 1) same-region compatible instances 2) smaller model in-region 3) cross-region with quantized model (only if route permits). Non-SLA routes may cross-region automatically.

Eli G.: Implementation detail: theres a flag "prefer_local_capacity". For Hosted tenants with SLOs, cross-region is blocked unless `allow_cross_region_burst` is set on the route.

Priya K.: @Eli can you paste the autoscaler snippet we showed so folks see exact fields?

Eli G.: Copied from playbook:

```
autoscaler:
  targets:
    - metric: gpu_utilization
      threshold: 0.7
  fallback:
    prefer_local_capacity: true
    cross_region_burst: false
    cross_region_whitelist: ["us-west1", "ap-southeast1"]
  burst_capacity:
    enabled: true
    max_extra_nodes: 10
```

Ben T.: Note: burst capacity uses spot/reserved inventory; if spots run out we attempt preemptible or committed nodes based on tenant tier. That explains short-lived bursts.

Olivia P.: From product: will cross-region bursts respect data residency rules? Enterprise EMEA tenants are region_locked.

Marta L.: Yes. region_locked tenants cannot cross-region. Routing layer enforces an allowlist check (internal docs at https://redwood.example.com/docs/ops/region-locking).

Sam R.: For teams: to enable cross-region with a quantized fallback, set route config: `allow_cross_region_burst: true` and `fallback_model: "gptx-small-q4"`. Ops will log and notify oncall.

Priya K.: If cross-region routing increases latency beyond SLO, does the system revert?

Eli G.: Yes 14 we have adaptive rollback: if 95p latency breaches configured SLO for >2 minutes, traffic shifts to the next policy (usually smaller in-region model or alternate region if allowed).

Ben T.: Action: infra will publish a latency matrix showing median/95p delta for cross-region fallbacks between us-west1 <-> eu-west3 and ap-southeast1. Im owning it, ETA EOD tomorrow.

Priya K.: One more: where do engineers place route overrides? Quick example?

Marta L.: Console -> Routes -> Edit -> Advanced. Example payload stored at `routes/<route>/config.json` with fields `allow_cross_region_burst`, `fallback_model`, `prefer_local_capacity`. Docs will include examples.

Sam R.: @deploy-bot any scheduled maintenance in eu-west3 that could affect H100 replenishment?

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance: eu-west3 kernel rollout at 1917080000 UTC. Expected 45m disruption for background nodes; critical-serving pools are cordoned.

Priya K.: Thanks everyone  Ben, Marta, Eli please follow up here with the matrix + exact doc links. Im summarizing in the All-Hands notes. :white_check_mark:

Ben T.: Will do.

Eli G.: Adding a short oncall runbook to infra wiki today.

Marta L.: Updating Console help text to surface these fields inline.

Priya K.: If anything from the live Q&A didnt get answered, drop a note here and well triage.
